status: source contract; not live world binding
decision: Gameplay need first, item second, lore/shop placement third. The fixed eight-items-per-shop quota is withdrawn.

campaignContract.purse: Use state.coins only; no preview purse or second currency.
campaignContract.save: Mutate through CWP21State.create(localStorage), campaign(nextState), project(); no new save key.
campaignContract.inventory: Use the existing state.items string array only for genuine carried items. Immediate meals and newspapers do not enter it.
campaignContract.ui: Use the existing notebook/leather dialog language, 44px controls, mobile focus return and confirmation pattern.
campaignContract.world: No shop is enabled until it has a verified walkable door, actor binding and return position. Market and Bakery holds remain unchanged.
campaignContract.compatibility: Existing saves initialise missing content.gear fields lazily. Owned unique gear cannot be bought twice. Full-health meals cannot charge the player.

supersedes.reason: Most additions had no live action, effect or requirement and were filler despite being trade-appropriate.

shops.title: Neighbourhood provisions
need: Recover health between street encounters without returning to Watch Igor.

shops.title: Boot and leather repair
shops.reason: Build 92 has no boot wear or repair loop; Watch boots are an assignment reward. The prototype wear model remains disabled.

shops.title: Clothing alterations
shops.reason: The existing Appearance editor is free and no purchasable wardrobe entitlement exists. Cloth cannot be sold as an inert bag item.

shops.title: Tools and household ironmongery
shops.reason: No crafting, household repair or equipment-durability action currently consumes tools, nails, hinges or rivets.

shops.title: Candles and lamp supplies
shops.reason: The carried lantern and street lighting have no fuel, wick or relighting state. Oil and tinder remain held until that mechanic exists.

shops.title: Paperbinder and stationer
shops.reason: The Watch Notebook and report filing do not consume paper, ink, wax or quills. Selling them would add bag clutter.

shops.title: Everyday apothecary
need: Treat combat injuries away from the Watch House.

shops.title: Second-hand household goods
need: Make one field treatment available each night without buying a consumable.

shops.title: Gimlet’s Hole Food Delicatessen
need: Recover health while patrolling the market and docks.

shops.title: Soon Shine Sun Shonky Shop
shops.reason: The current Appearance editor is free and no second-hand garment ownership layer exists.

shops.title: Burleigh & Stronginthearm
need: Improve lawful close-combat capability after the player has earned enough coin.

shops.title: Wienrich and Boettcher
shops.reason: There is no gift, relationship or confection use. Luxury chocolate is not reduced to a cheap healing potion to justify stock.

shops.title: Boffo Novelty and Joke Shop
shops.reason: No current case requires a disguise, and appearance changes must not create false infiltration or impersonation powers.

shops.title: Poleforth’s Newsagents and Tobacconist
need: Read and clip the current edition into the Watch Notebook.

shops.title: Drayman’s Butchers
shops.reason: The game has no cooking or camp-provision system. Raw butcher orders are not treated as instant health items.

shops.title: Pointer & Pickles
shops.reason: No mineral collection or analysis loop exists. The Investigator’s magnifier remains an assignment reward rather than a reason to sell samples.

shops.title: Shatta
shops.reason: Premium fashion is not yet connected to owned wardrobe pieces; the free Appearance editor must not be charged for indirectly.

shops.title: Ironcrust’s Bakery
shops.reason: No dwarf-specific food adapter or lawful improvised-weapon rule exists. Dwarf bread receives no automatic healing or combat statistics.

shops.title: Laughing Falafel, Klatchistan Take-Away and All Nite Grocery
need: Provide a night-patrol meal when other counters may be closed.

shops.title: Crumley’s
shops.reason: The present game has no gifting, toy collection or authored case that requires a toy.

shops.title: Hugos · historical-name candidate
shops.reason: Grooming is not an owned service and the existing Appearance editor remains free. No paid duplicate is introduced.
